author: Vox
description:
Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon overcame a 17-to-1 fundraising gap to win the state’s Democratic Senate primary. Can she score another upset victory in November? 

In this special episode of America, Actually, Nixon joins Vox’s Astead Herndon to break down her primary win, her progressive policy stance, and her strategy to become Florida’s next US Senator.  

00:00 How Angie Nixon pulled off a stunning upset
01:55 The grassroots strategy that powered her victory
03:38 Can progressive policies win statewide in Florida?
07:01 From union organizer to Senate candidate
11:06 Why progressives struggle to reach Black voters
14:35 Nixon on Israel, Gaza, and supporting BDS
16:39 Policing, public safety, DEI, and reparations
22:49 The Democratic establishment, DSA, and the socialist label

America, Actually publishes video episodes every Saturday tackling key issues in politics, culture, and the economy. Subscribe to Vox’s YouTube channel to get them. Listen to episodes of America, Actually on A
title: Angie Nixon’s playbook to be Florida’s next senator | America, Actually

author: Vox
description:
Down where the light starts to fade — between around 30 and 150 meters below the ocean surface — there are mysterious "mesophotic coral ecosystems," also known as "deep reefs." 

These ecosystems are hard to dive down into, and therefore hard to study, so we still don’t know much about them. Like even what creatures live there.

To learn more, Luiz Rocha, a curator of ichthyology at the California Academy of Sciences, dove down into the depths in Palau, Guam, the Marshall Islands, and French Polynesia between 2016 and 2018 and left behind scientific devices known as ARMS (Autonomous Reef Monitoring Structures).

Those structures spent almost a decade becoming encrusted with deep reef life, slowly turning into mini versions of the reefs themselves. Earlier this year, Rocha and colleagues from several institutions returned to Palau to retrieve the ARMS and unwrap them like scientific presents.

Vox's Byrd Pinkerton, host of the Unexplainable podcast, went along to watch that process. Re
title: Scientific "unboxing" of a mysterious underwater world
